key_insight: LDT-Coord uses a lightweight digital twin to coordinate heterogeneous embodied LLM agents without relying on multi-round dialogue, cutting communication overhead while preserving task success.
engineering_relevance: The framework is directly relevant to smart factories, warehouses, and service robotics where distributed agents must coordinate reliably under limited network and compute resources.
method: Each agent chooses an action locally and reports the action plus a structured temporal constraint to the DT server.
A rule-based, training-free orchestrator in the digital twin resolves resource conflicts and sends back coordination instructions.
Communication is further minimized by framing reporting as a constrained POMDP and optimizing it with PPO-Lagrangian.
evidence_signal: Simulation results in the abstract report task success comparable to conventional methods while reducing communication overhead by more than 70× and remaining robust to LLM heterogeneity.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate structured constraints and digital-twin orchestration, so real-world performance may degrade if the DT model or resource descriptions are imperfect.
paper_title: Communication-Efficient Digital-Twin Coordination for Heterogeneous LLM Embodied Agents over Computing Power Networks
